subject: Re: Nebula MSA redlines - uptime floor, credits, and maintenance windows
messages:
From: Erin O'Leary <erin@nebula.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebula.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines - uptime floor and credits

Hi Naomi / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft MSA. Attaching Nebula's redlines (see: Nebula_MSA_redline_20260927.docx). A few highlights we want to flag up front so you can triage internally:

- We need an explicit uptime "floor" of 99.95% global with regional measurement; anything below that triggers the credit staircase.
- Procurement wants a clear cap on cumulative credits per 12-month period (they propose 10% of ARR).
- Maintenance windows: Nebula asks for a 4-hour weekly window per region with a 30-day notice for planned blackouts, and an emergency patch carveout that doesn't count as downtime if within a documented security remediation.
- Incident response: they want a P1 response within 15 minutes and remediation TTR defined (they propose 4 hours).

Could you confirm which of these are negotiable and which are showstoppers? We also copied Jake from engineering in case we need quick clarification on maintenance windows.

Thanks,
Erin
Procurement | Nebula AI

Attachments: Nebula_MSA_redline_20260927.docx (docx, 42KB)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Erin O'Leary <erin@nebula.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines - uptime floor and credits

Thanks Erin — got the doc and flagged the items internally. Quick note on process: we'll circulate a counter-proposal that separates commercial credit policy (what Sales can offer) from technical definitions (what Ops measures). That keeps legal/finance and engineering alignment clean.

Next steps from my side:
- I will summarize the redline asks into a short decision matrix and highlight anything that requires an approved credit cap exception.
- Marissa, please confirm legal's position on the 10% ARR cap and whether we can propose a sliding cap tied to committed spend.
- Rachel/Connor, can you confirm whether a 4-hour weekly maintenance window per region is operationally feasible and whether security patches qualify for the "emergency carveout" Erin describes?

Expect a draft response by EOD Tuesday.

—Naomi
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline-summary-naomi-20260928.pdf (will attach after internal draft)

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines - legal take and proposed concessions

Quick legal read — high level thoughts below. I copied Legal Counsel in thread for formal redline guidance but wanted to surface negotiation levers: 

1) Credit cap: 10% ARR absolute cap is risky for us. We can offer a tiered cap: 5% of ARR for accounts under $250k ARR, 10% for $250k–$2M, and 15% for >$2M with an aggregated annual ceiling. That gives sales more flexibility for high-commit deals.

2) Uptime measurement & floor: we should push for a 30-day rolling window measured per region with a single global metric only as a convenience. Also propose a narrow list of exclusions (force majeure, customer-caused outages, scheduled maintenance with notice).

3) Maintenance windows: agree to scheduled weekly windows but limit to 2 x 3-hour windows (region-local midnight preferred) instead of 4 hours. For emergency security patches we can accept an exclusion if we provide a post-patch impact report.

4) Incident SLAs: legal prefers response times (acknowledgement) be contractual and remediation be a best-effort target. If Sales wants remediation commitments, it must be tied to higher tiers/credits.

I'll draft specific language suggested for the order form and mark the clauses in redline. If Sales wants to keep their counter to 10% cap, we should route to Finance for an approved exception before sending back to Nebula.

—Marissa
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: (legal will provide marked redline separately)

From: rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines - ops feasibility

Operational notes from the runtime team:

- Maintenance windows: We can commit to weekly windows but 4 hours is heavy for some APAC regions; 2 x 3-hour windows aligned to local off-peak is more realistic. We'll standardize on a 30-day rolling calendar for planned maintenance notices.

- Emergency patches: Security patches that require immediate rollout will be scheduled outside the regular window if severity is CVSS >= 9.0 or if exploit is in the wild. These rollouts should be documented and excluded from uptime calculations if we can show change logs + rollback capability within 72 hours.

- Measurement: We'll provide both region-level and global aggregated metrics (ISO timestamps, per-region availability logs). We recommend a 5-minute probe granularity for measurement.

- Credits: From an operational POV, credits calculated on per-minute unavailability can be noisy — we prefer stair-step thresholds (e.g., <99.95 -> x%, <99.5 -> y%).

Happy to walk through with Nebula engineering (Jake) tomorrow morning PST to sync on blackout scheduling.

—Rachel
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Attachment: ops-maintenance-patterns.pdf (attachment stub)

From: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines - incident categorization and response

A couple of clarifications on incident SLA semantics to include in the counter: 

- Response vs remediation: We'll accept a contractual "response" SLA (P1 ack within 15 minutes) but remediation time should be an objective Tier Target, not a contractual penalty, unless Nebula takes a premium support package. For P1 remediation we can commit to a 4-hour Target Response Time (TRT) as a measurable objective.

- Escalation path: Include an ops contact, on-call rotation, and an executive SLA breach notification after 4 hours of unresolved P1. That buys us time to triage without immediate credit triggers.

- Rollbacks/blackouts: We will attempt automated rollback for failed config pushes; if rollback is required and completes within the TRT window, it should not count against availability.

I'll draft proposed incident language for Marissa to include in the order form redlines.

—Connor
Sr. Manager, Support Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident-sla-template.txt (stub)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Erin O'Leary <erin@nebula.ai>, Jake Morris <jake@nebula.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>, procurement@nebula.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines - uptime floor and credits (proposed counter)

Hi Erin & team — thanks for the patience while we reviewed. Attached is a short counter-summary (redline-summary-naomi-20260928.pdf) and our proposed positions below so you can share with Procurement and Engineering: 

1) Uptime & measurement: We will provide region-level and global metrics with 5-minute probe granularity. Proposed contractual floor: 99.95% measured on a 30-day rolling basis per region.

2) Credits & cap: We cannot accept a flat 10% ARR cap across the board. Proposed commercial structure: tiered cap by committed ARR (5% / 10% / 15%) with an absolute annual ceiling equal to 15% of ARR unless a special commercial exception is approved by Finance.

3) Maintenance windows & emergency carveouts: We propose 2 x 3-hour weekly maintenance windows aligned to local off-peak hours per region. Emergency security patches (CVSS >= 9.0 or active exploit) may be deployed outside these windows if we provide a post-deploy impact report within 72 hours; such events are excluded from uptime calculations if rollback within 72 hours is documented.

4) Incident SLAs: Contractual response (acknowledge P1 within 15 minutes). Remediation will be a Target Response Time (TRT) of 4 hours for P1 as an objective; credit triggers tied to availability tiers, not remediation time. Escalation notifications to execs after 4 hours unresolved.

5) Next steps: Marissa will propose exact redline language for the order form and MSA (we will mark exclusions and exceptions). If Nebula wants to negotiate a different credit cap, please provide a target ARR band and we will route to Finance for an exception.

If that's acceptable, can we schedule a 30-minute call Thursday 9:00 AM PST with Jake and our ops leads to align on blackout windows and measurement endpoints?

Thanks,
Naomi
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline-summary-naomi-20260928.pdf (summary, 18KB)
